cards.q: If we were to convert an RGB colour image to 8-bit greyscale using the lightness method, what greyscale value would be produced for a pixel with the RGB triplet (32,176,202)? Round any answer ∈ ℝ/ℕ to be ∈ ℕ, and round .5 upwards. Formula: L(i,j) = (max(R, G, B) + min(R, G, B)) ÷ 2
method: Pick the largest and the smallest of the three channel values. Ignore the middle one.
Add them and divide by 2.
If the result ends in .5, round it up to the next whole number.
cards.check: The answer lies between the smallest and the largest channel value, exactly half way.
cards.trap: Using all three values. That is the average method in card 2. Lightness uses only the largest and the smallest.

cards.q: If we were to convert an RGB colour image to 8-bit greyscale using the average method, what greyscale value would be produced for a pixel with the RGB triplet (227,117,111)? Round any answer ∈ ℝ/ℕ to be ∈ ℕ, and round .5 upwards. Formula: L(i,j) = (R + G + B) ÷ 3
method: Add the three channel values.
Divide by 3.
Round to the nearest whole number.
cards.check: The answer lies between the smallest and the largest channel value.
cards.trap: Cutting the decimals off. 151.67 becomes 152, not 151.

cards.q: If we were to convert an RGB colour image to 8-bit greyscale using the luminosity method, what greyscale value would be produced for a pixel with the RGB triplet (155,252,67)? Round any fractional value to the nearest integer, and round .5 upwards. Formula: L(i,j) = 0.21R + 0.72G + 0.07B
method: Multiply red by 0.21, green by 0.72 and blue by 0.07. Write the three products down.
Add the three products.
Round the total to the nearest whole number. Round once, at the end.
cards.check: The three weights add up to 1, so the answer lies between the smallest and the largest channel value. Green has the largest weight, so the answer sits closest to the green value.
cards.trap: You entered 210, and the answer is 219. Write the three products on paper (32.55, 181.44, 4.69) and add them again before typing. Keep the weights in the order red 0.21, green 0.72, blue 0.07.
cards.unsure: Canvas did not show the correct answer. 219 comes from the formula. The capture does not show how 210 was reached. Reading 03 has a worked example, (100,150,5), that prints 130 where the formula gives 129.35. The quiz wording says nearest integer, so this card follows the quiz. For these numbers rounding to nearest and rounding up both give 219.

cards.q: Convert the greyscale image matrix L, below, to a binary image matrix, B, using a threshold value T = 119 (which is sRGB middle grey). Formula: B(i,j) = 0 if L(i,j) < T, 1 else
cards.varies: Only one attempt was captured, so this is not confirmed. In Quiz 02 the Fill in the Blank questions kept the same numbers every attempt. The test may use a different matrix or T.
method: Write the test next to the matrix: 0 if L < T, otherwise 1.
Go through the pixels one at a time. A pixel below T becomes 0.
A pixel equal to T or above T becomes 1.
cards.check: The output has only 0s and 1s and the same shape as L. Dark pixels are 0 and bright pixels are 1.
cards.trap: Giving 0 to a pixel that is equal to T. The test is strictly less than, so a pixel equal to T becomes 1.

cards.q: The minimum number of bars that can appear on an image histogram of a binary image is ___ and the maximum number of bars is ___. The minimum number of bars that can appear on an image histogram of an 8-bit greyscale image is ___ and the maximum number of bars is ___.
cards.ans: Binary: minimum 1, maximum 2. 8-bit greyscale: minimum 1, maximum 256.
cards.varies: Only one attempt was captured, so this is not confirmed. The question looks fixed. The test may ask about a different bit depth.
method: A histogram has one bar for each pixel value that is present in the image.
The minimum is 1. That happens when every pixel has the same value.
The maximum is the number of possible values. That is 2 for binary and 2^b for a b-bit image. For 8-bit, 2⁸ = 256.
cards.check: The maximum number of bars equals the number of shades from Quiz 01, v = 2^t.
cards.trap: You entered 8 for the 8-bit maximum. 8 is the number of bits. The number of possible values is 2⁸ = 256, from 0 to 255.

working: Binary: values 0 and 1, so at most 2 bars and at least 1.
8-bit greyscale: values 0 to 255, so at most 2⁸ = 256 bars and at least 1.

cards.unsure: Canvas did not show the correct value for the last blank. 256 follows from Reading 03, which says each greyscale pixel may assume one of 256 levels.

cards.q: Below is a 3-bit greyscale image (thus with possible grey levels from 0..7). Enter the values for its count histogram.
cards.varies: Only one attempt was captured, so this is not confirmed. Cards 6 to 9 all use this same matrix. The test may use a different matrix.
method: Write the levels 0 to 7 in a column.
Go through the matrix one pixel at a time and put a tally mark next to its level. Cross each pixel off as you go.
Count the tally marks for each level.
cards.check: The counts add up to MN. Here 3 + 5 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 5 + 4 + 1 = 25 = 5 × 5.
cards.trap: Counting level by level and missing a pixel. Tally pixel by pixel, then add the counts. A total that is not MN means a miscount.

working: Level 0 appears 3 times, level 1 appears 5 times, level 2 appears 3 times, level 3 appears 2 times.
Level 4 appears 2 times, level 5 appears 5 times, level 6 appears 4 times, level 7 appears 1 time.

cards.q: Below is a 3-bit greyscale image (thus with possible grey levels from 0..7). Enter the values for its normalised count histogram to 2 decimal places (2 dp).
cards.varies: Same matrix as card 6. Not confirmed across attempts.
method: Build the count histogram as in card 6.
Divide every count by MN.
Round each value to 2 decimal places.
cards.check: The normalised counts add up to 1.
cards.trap: Dividing by the number of levels (8) or by the largest count. The divisor is the number of pixels, MN = 25.

cards.q: Below is a 3-bit greyscale image (thus with possible grey levels from 0..7). Enter the values for its cumulative count histogram.
cards.varies: Same matrix as card 6. Not confirmed across attempts.
method: Build the count histogram as in card 6.
The first cumulative value is the first count.
For each next level, add its count to the cumulative value above it.
cards.check: The values never go down. The last value is MN, which is 25 here.
cards.trap: Entering the plain counts again. Each cumulative value is the count of that level plus all the levels before it.

cards.q: Below is a 3-bit greyscale image (thus with possible grey levels from 0..7). Enter the values for its normalised cumulative count histogram to 2 decimal places (2 dp).
cards.varies: Same matrix as card 6. Not confirmed across attempts.
method: Build the cumulative count histogram as in card 8.
Divide every cumulative value by MN.
Round each value to 2 decimal places.
cards.check: The values never go down. The last value is exactly 1.
cards.trap: Adding up the rounded normalised counts from card 7. Rounding errors can build up that way. Divide the whole-number cumulative counts by MN.

cards.q: Perform low-pass thresholding to produce a binary image B from 8-bit greyscale image L using threshold value T = 64. Formula: B(i,j) = 1 if L(i,j) ≤ T, 0 else
cards.varies: Only one attempt was captured, so this is not confirmed. Cards 10 to 13 and 15 use this same matrix with different thresholds. The test may change the matrix or T.
method: Write the test next to the matrix: 1 if L ≤ T.
Go through the pixels one at a time. Write 1 where the test is true and 0 where it is false.
Low-pass lets the low (dark) values pass, so the dark pixels become 1.
cards.check: Count the pixels that are ≤ T. The mask has that many 1s. Here only 15 and 12 pass, so there are two 1s.
cards.trap: Marking the bright pixels as 1. That is high-pass. A pixel equal to T also passes, because the test is ≤.

working: Row 1: 197, 160 and 150 are all above 64, so 0, 0, 0.
Row 3: 92, 200 and 115 are all above 64, so 0, 0, 0.

cards.q: Perform high-pass thresholding to produce a binary image B from 8-bit greyscale image L using threshold value T = 100. Formula: B(i,j) = 1 if L(i,j) ≥ T, 0 else
cards.varies: Same matrix as card 10 with a different T. Not confirmed across attempts.
method: Same steps as card 10. The test changes to: 1 if L ≥ T.
High-pass lets the high (bright) values pass, so the bright pixels become 1.
cards.check: Count the pixels that are ≥ T. The mask has that many 1s. Here six pixels pass.
cards.trap: Reusing the T from the question before. Each question gives its own T. Here T = 100, so 115 passes and 92 fails.

cards.q: Perform band-pass thresholding on image matrix L using threshold values T₁ = 64, T₂ = 100 to produce a binary image (mask). Formula: B(i,j) = 1 if L(i,j) ≥ T₁ ∧ L(i,j) ≤ T₂, 0 else
cards.varies: Same matrix as card 10 with two thresholds. Not confirmed across attempts.
method: Same steps as card 10. The test changes to: 1 if T₁ ≤ L ≤ T₂.
The ∧ symbol means AND. A pixel must pass both parts, so it must sit inside the band from T₁ to T₂.
cards.check: Every pixel marked 1 has a value from T₁ to T₂. Here only 92 is between 64 and 100.
cards.trap: Marking the pixels outside the band. That is band-reject. A pixel equal to T₁ or T₂ is inside the band and becomes 1.

working: Row 2: 15 is below 64, 208 is above 100, 12 is below 64, so 0, 0, 0.
Row 3: 92 is between 64 and 100 so 1, 200 gives 0, 115 gives 0.

cards.q: Perform band-reject thresholding on image matrix L using threshold values T₁ = 120, T₂ = 180 to produce a binary image (mask). Formula: B(i,j) = 1 if L(i,j) ≤ T₁ ∨ L(i,j) ≥ T₂, 0 else
cards.varies: Same matrix as card 10 with two thresholds. Not confirmed across attempts.
method: Same steps as card 10. The test changes to: 1 if L ≤ T₁ or L ≥ T₂.
The ∨ symbol means OR. A pixel passes if it is at or below T₁, or at or above T₂.
Fast way: find the pixels strictly between T₁ and T₂ and write 0 there. Write 1 everywhere else.
cards.check: Every pixel marked 0 has a value strictly between T₁ and T₂. Here only 160 and 150 are between 120 and 180.
cards.trap: Mixing up ∧ and ∨. Also, a pixel equal to T₁ or T₂ becomes 1 here as well, so band-reject is not the exact opposite of band-pass at those two values.

working: Row 1: 197 ≥ 180 gives 1, 160 and 150 are between 120 and 180 so 0, 0.

cards.q: We can use multi-band thresholding to select colour objects from an RGB image, which entails thresholding the red, green and blue channels are combining results. Given the RGB image below, enter the binary image mask, M, produced by applying the following multiband threshold operation where T₁ = 128, T₂ = 128, T₃ = 48: S(i,j) = 1 if (R(i,j) < T₁) ∧ (G(i,j) > T₂) ∧ (B(i,j) > T₃), 0 else
cards.varies: Only one attempt was captured, so this is not confirmed. The test may change the channel values, the thresholds or the direction of each test.
method: Read the three tests and note the direction of each one. Here red must be below T₁, green above T₂ and blue above T₃.
Test the red channel. Cross out every place that fails.
Test green only at the places still left. Cross out the failures. Then do the same for blue.
Write 1 at the places that passed all three tests and 0 everywhere else.
cards.check: Pick one place marked 1 and check all three of its channel values against the tests. Here place (2,1) has R = 80 < 128, G = 190 > 128 and B = 160 > 48.
cards.trap: Giving 1 to a place that passes only one or two tests. All three must pass. The tests here are strict (< and >), so a value equal to its threshold fails.

working: R < 128 passes at every place except (2,2), where R = 160.
G > 128 passes only at (2,1) with 190 and (2,3) with 160.
B > 48 at those two places: 160 and 120 both pass.

cards.unsure: The question text names the mask M in one place and S in the formula. That is the tutor's wording. They are the same mask.

cards.q: Apply low-pass thresholding with T = 100 to image L, below, and use the binary mask produced, B, to select pixels (i.e., isolate the object of interest). Formula: L′(i,j) = L(i,j) if B(i,j) = 1, 0 else
cards.varies: Same matrix as card 10. Not confirmed across attempts. The test may change T or the type of threshold.
method: Make the mask B with the low-pass test from card 10: 1 if L ≤ T.
Where B is 1, copy the original grey value from L.
Where B is 0, write 0. This is the same as the entry-wise product L ∘ B from Quiz 02.
cards.check: Every value in the answer is either 0 or an original value from L that passes the test.
cards.trap: Entering the mask (1s and 0s). The answer holds grey values and 0s. Here 115 is above 100, so it becomes 0.

working: Keep 15, 12 and 92. Every other place becomes 0.
